Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11175 of 2023
Applicant :- Pappu

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Akhilesh Kumar,Urmila Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Akhilesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned
Brief Holder for the State-respondent.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 183
of 2021, under Sections 406 & 420 Ipc, Police Station Lalauli, District Fatehpur, during pendency of
the trial in the court below.

Fir of the present case was lodged under sections 406, 409 & 420 Ipc against the applicant and ten
others and according to the Fir the then Village Pradhan and Village Panchayat Adhikari, illegally
transferred the huge amount to applicant and other co-accused persons and it is alleged that Rs.
60,000/- was given to the applicant and the money which was alleged to have been transferred was
for construction of toilet.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant
are totally false and baseless and applicant did not involve in any misappropriation of public fund
and it appears even from the perusal of Fir that principal accused in the present matter is
co-accused Krishna Kant Singh and Ramesh Chandra Gihar the then village pradhan and Gram

. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 21.2.2023,
therefore, he may be released on bail.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and conceded that principal accused in the present matter appears to be co-accused Krishna Kant Singh and Ramesh Chandra Gihar the then village Pradhan and Village Panchayat Adhikari, respectively and applicant appears to be the person who received Rs. 60,000/- and he is not having any criminal history.

He could not dispute the fact that it is no where stated either in the FIR or in the statement of the witness that why Rs. 60,000/-
was given to the applicant.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

Although, there is allegation against the applicant that the then Village Pradhan and Village Panchayat Adhikari provided him Rs. 60,000/- but it did not mention in the FIR that why they gave Rs. 60,000/- to the applicant.
On the other hand, applicant has come with specific defence that he is a labour and he did some labour work for construction of road and the amount of Rs. 60,000/- was given to him as his labour.
He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 21.2.2023, therefore, he may be released on bail.
Therefore, from the discussions made above, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Pappu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
